--- title: "Welcome to the NFL Preseason! Let's look at key players fighting to start" date: "2026-08-27" author: - "Nick Giangreco" freeze: true vignette: > %\VignetteIndexEntry{Welcome to the NFL Preseason! Let's look at key players fighting to start} %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html} %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8} --- ::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"} This is the first blog post of this website! Please bear with us as we get our bearings and set things up. But I couldn't resist starting to look at some football data! ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} *Data as of the `data-latest` release, retrieved 2026-08-27. Both players' NFL careers are ongoing, so late seasons reflect roster presence in the current data and may extend further.* ::: I am a Buffalo Bills fan. I'll admit, I do not watch as many games as I should. However, I always cheer on the Bills from afar: celebrating their victories, hoping for the best following losses, and wishing them well as the team grows and does good in the Buffalo community. I am just a lowly data scientist, who rather explore data than watch football on TV. Previous data projects I have done included investigating NFL data exclusively, but this project intends to look at player's trajectories through their college career, the NFL draft, and their NFL career. While this is a large endeavor, this website is dedicated for achieving that objective over time. I am also looking forward to seeing improvement in my communication and data storytelling. In that spirit, I want to start investigating players playing tonight in the home-opener preseason game between the Buffalo Bills and Pittsburgh Steelers. Specifically, Shane Buechele who is starting and Kyle Allen who is also vying for the QB2 position right behind Josh Allen. ## Origins of Shane Buechele and Kyle Allen ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Cleaned recruiting schema (decision 0018): raw athleteId/name/year/committedTo/ # ranking are now playerId/recruit_name/hs_class/committed_to/national_rank, and # hometown (city/stateProvince) is not carried. The recruiting id is an # untrusted namespace (decision 0013); this direct filter is QA-verified for # these two named players, not a general-purpose join. open_dataset("data/recruiting.parquet") |> filter(playerId %in% subjects$cfb_athlete_id) |> select( playerId, recruit_name, hs_class, committed_to, recruit_position, stars, rating, national_rank ) |> collect() |> arrange(desc(stars)) |> kable(caption = "High-school recruiting profiles (CFBD).") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: High-school recruiting profiles (CFBD). |playerId |recruit_name | hs_class|committed_to |recruit_position | stars| rating| national_rank| |:--------|:--------------|--------:|:------------|:----------------|-----:|------:|-------------:| |559681 |Kyle Allen | 2014|Texas A&M |PRO | 5| 0.9956| 8| |4039034 |Shane Buechele | 2016|Texas |DUAL | 4| 0.9250| 182| ::: ::: Unfortunately, I'm not very well versed in high school football rating. But at first glance it looks like Kyle Allen was a more promising prospect early in his career compared to Shane Buechele. ## Teams of Shane Buechele and Kyle Allen Let's see where they went to where they are now: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p <- ggplot(spine, aes(x = season, y = who)) + geom_tile_interactive( aes(fill = color, tooltip = tooltip, data_id = paste(who, season)), color = "white", height = 0.7 ) + geom_from_path(aes(path = logo), height = 0.11) + scale_fill_identity() + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(min(spine$season), max(spine$season), 1)) + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_cfbstats(base_size = 14) + theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "none") girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9, height_svg = 3.5) ``` ::: {#fig-timeline .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` Team by season, college through the NFL, in each team's brand colors and logos. Hover any tile for the team and season. Neither player appears in the NFL draft-pick records — both entered undrafted. ::: ::: Both players have had a pretty good run in alot of good teams! Interestingly, what this figure doesn't tell you is that both players were not in the NFL draft. Both were free agents and picked up by NFL teams. This was seen when neither players have data records in the draft data. ## Good luck to Shane Buechele and Kyle Allen! There's so much more to look into, like how much they played, their statistics when they played, their injuries, et cetera. But, alas, that will be for another day after much thinking with my partner. But this short post was a great look into some of the data and a type of visualization of these player's trajectory!
